title: U.S. House · Texas's 25th Congressional District
area: North-central Texas, spanning from Tarrant County (Fort Worth area) north into rural counties along I-35.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.
In the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, Dione Sims defeated William Marks, 60.5% to 39.5%. Roger Williams was unopposed in the Republican primary.

positions.summary: Official site issues page says he opposes universal background checks, buy-backs, assault weapons bans and red flag laws.
positions.quote: oppose universal background checks, buy-backs, assault weapons bans, and red flag laws

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and chairs the House Committee on Small Business in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Dione Sims
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 60.5% of the vote

priorities.text: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey, said she is passionate about protecting democracy, expanding access to affordable healthcare, economic dignity for working families, criminal justice reform, mental health, and civil and human rights.
Said she is running to help Congress 'reclaim its constitutional role' and restore checks and balances against unchecked executive power.
Said she would fight for living wages, strong public schools, and an economy that works for working people.

positions.summary: Her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, says she would strengthen the ACA and expand Medicaid.
positions.quote: strengthening the ACA, expanding Medicaid, and protecting coverage for preexisting conditions

statements.quote: I will oppose policies that cut benefits or raise costs, and I will protect reproductive care.
statements.context: On her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia (2026)

statements.quote: affordability begins with a living wage. I will fight to raise pay, protect the right to organize, and crack down on wage theft
statements.context: On her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia (2026)

statements.quote: My immigration policy is rooted in dignity, due process, and keeping families together. I support a roadmap to citizenship for long-time immigrants, including Dreamers and Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders, along with safe, orderly border management.
statements.context: On her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia (2026)

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from her campaign website text as reproduced on Ballotpedia; her own site (dionesimsforcongress.com) loads its issue text with JavaScript and was not read directly.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Texas, 2026

researchNotes: Williams' positions are limited to official committee assignments; no 2026 Candidate Connection survey or campaign-site statements were found for him at research time. Federal key votes and FEC totals for the incumbent are added separately by script. Public biographical information about Dione Sims is limited to her Ballotpedia profile and Candidate Connection survey; no independent news profile was found.
